name: Corydalis

project_scope.source_pool_reference: C. curvisiliqua subsp. curvisiliqua: taxonomy-review comparison only; not installed

look_here_first: Recognize the finely divided alternate leaves and bilaterally symmetrical yellow flower with a rearward spur. For species ID, search for tiny closed self-pollinating racemes and measure several mature seeds: C. micrantha ~1.5 mm, C. aurea nearly 2 mm.

shared_traits: Small herbs with alternate finely divided foliage and racemes of spurred bilateral flowers.
Four petals, one outer petal spurred, six stamens in two bundles, two-valved capsules containing dark seeds.
Yellow color, delicate leaves and capsule length overlap between the two species.
priority: Ripe seed diameter measured with millimeter scale
Seed sculpture and marginal ring, with subspecies caution
Mature capsule angle and primary raceme height as supporting characters
study_strategy.warning: Do not identify by capsule angle or raceme height alone: C. aurea subsp. occidentalis may have erect capsules; C. micrantha subspecies vary in fruit length.
look_here_first: Confirm Corydalis from alternate divided foliage and a side-on spurred bilateral flower.
Check the same plant for tiny cleistogamous racemes; their presence supports C. micrantha, absence is not decisive.
Measure several ripe seeds: C. micrantha about 1.5 mm versus C. aurea nearly 2 mm; inspect marginal ring and surface texture.
Treat fruit posture and flower length as supporting only; retain Corydalis sp. if seeds and cleistogamy cannot be assessed.

species_comparison_matrix.aurea: Narrow ring present or absent by subspecies

comparison_cards.title: C. aurea vs C. micrantha
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Compare closed-flower racemes and ripe seeds before fruit orientation.
comparison_cards.caution: Cleistogamous flowers can be absent on individual C. micrantha. Seed margin and capsule orientation vary within C. aurea.

quick_key.if: Tiny closed-flower racemes and ripe seeds around 1.5 mm
Ripe seeds nearly 2 mm, essentially smooth, closed-flower racemes rare
Ripe seed surface distinctly rough under magnification
quick_key.then: Compare C. curvisiliqua; taxonomy review required

quick_key.if: No ripe seed or useful racemes

overlap_and_cautions: Flower color, leaf shape, capsule length and flower length overlap.
C. aurea subsp. occidentalis may have erect fruits and racemes above leaves.
C. micrantha subsp. texensis may have long fruits.
FNA separates C. curvisiliqua from C. aurea by distinctly rough versus essentially smooth seed surfaces; source-pool name requires concept mapping.

local_lookalikes.separation: Distinctly rough ripe seeds under magnification versus essentially smooth C. aurea; compare size and cleistogamy to C. micrantha.
Spurred petal 7–9 mm and incurved ~2 mm spur, versus 11–16 mm and 4–7 mm spur in this pair.

diagnostic_photo_checklist.need: Whole plants with upper leaves and primary raceme visible
C. micrantha open and tiny closed racemes on same plant, arrows to bracts
Both species, 3+ seeds each, calibrated 1 mm scale
Identical magnification showing seed sculpture/marginal ring; authenticated curvisiliqua comparison only
Intact fruiting racemes, pedicels, curvature and posture
Side-view open flowers with ruler, labeled outer petal and spur

genus_diagnostics.look_here_first: SEE: finely divided alternate foliage and yellow spurred flowers → SPOT: side-view rearward spur and two-valved capsule → NAME: spur, raceme, cleistogamous flower, seed → COMPARE: tiny closed racemes and calibrated ripe seeds → REMEMBER: flower color and capsule posture overlap.

shared_structure_examples.plain: A pouch-like backward extension behind one of the four petals, best seen from the side.
shared_structure_examples.where_to_look: Trace the back of an open flower from the petal to the spur tip; distinguish the spur from its supporting stalk.
shared_structure_examples.photo_role: same-scale side-on open flower macro for each species, with 1 mm ruler

shared_structure_examples.plain: A flower-bearing stalk; some tiny flowers stay closed and pollinate themselves.
shared_structure_examples.where_to_look: Look for a second, much smaller flower cluster on a C. micrantha plant, alongside normal open flowers.
shared_structure_examples.photo_role: one authenticated C. micrantha plant with open and closed racemes, matching C. aurea view

shared_structure_examples.plain: An elongated dry fruit that opens along two sides to release seeds.
shared_structure_examples.where_to_look: Follow a flower stalk to a mature fruit and show the capsule tip, attachment and orientation.
shared_structure_examples.photo_role: matched intact mature fruiting racemes for both species

shared_structure_examples.plain: Tiny ripe seeds are measured across their width; some have a narrow raised edge.
shared_structure_examples.where_to_look: Compare at least three fully ripe seeds per plant under equal magnification and an actual millimeter scale.
shared_structure_examples.photo_role: authenticated mature seeds both species, calibrated macro/microscope; curvisiliqua only after taxon review
